newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee continues roller-coaster ride.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee continues roller-coaster ride.

text.p: Vietnam's robusta coffee trade continued a roller-coaster ride this week thanks to world market volatility, with prices fluctuating more than $110 a tonne.
Dealers said trade had been active on both the export and internal markets, with farmers seeking to capitalise on generally higher prices by selling.

The FOB Saigon Port price for Vietnamese robusta was quoted at between $1,380 and $1,490 earlier in the week, before settling at around the $1,400 mark late on Thursday. Few deals were taking place on Friday.
A week ago coffee was trading at around $1,320 per tonne.

Market rumours that Indonesian exporters were buying coffee from Vietnam for re-export could not be confirmed. Dealers said there had been some signs of this happening in early February, but none since then.

Vietnam has exported around 180-200,000 tonnes of coffee so far from its 1996/97 harvest. Traders estimate that between 60-80,000 tonnes is still left, of which 10-20,000 tonnes has been committed over the past couple of weeks.
World coffee prices have soared recently, climbing 50 percent in New York since the start of the year and 15 percent over the past week before slipping on Thursday.
Regional traders said they were expecting a further downward correction in New York futures on Friday.
"New York could come down to 190 to 180 today, but later we're expecting a further trend to the upside," one dealer said.
He added that London was currently undervalued and arbitrage was therefore likely to come in to play.
